candidate.answerReason: The round trip covers 2 kilometers in 40 minutes, or two-thirds of an hour. Total distance divided by total time is 3 km/hr, agreeing with choice A.

methods.label: Use total distance and total time
methods.explanation:
Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total travel time. Mary walks the same \(1\)-km route in each direction, so the round-trip distance is \(2\) km.

The total time is \(30+10=40\) minutes, which is \(40/60=2/3\) hour. Therefore her average speed is
\[
\frac{2}{2/3}=3\text{ km/hr}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{3\text{ km/hr}}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses the elementary definition of average speed, time conversion, and fraction division.

needsNewNodes.description: For a journey with positive total duration, calculate average speed as total distance traveled divided by total elapsed time. Combine distances and times across all legs and express them in consistent units.
